pass_a_gloss: …meditation, long-suffering, endurance. 'He blessed your sons in you', who are the faithful infants, those that received the Lord with the branches, that is, with new fruits, those sucking the milk of the teaching of Christ; for believing in him at once they praise, they hymn, they glorify, as it has been written: 'Out of the mouth of infants and sucklings you prepared praise.' Let us become for him a holy vehicle instead of an unclean colt, in order that he may mount upon us. Let us yoke to him the chariot of our thoughts, 'and he will reign' upon us 'into the ages, and of his kingdom there will not be an end.' Let us take a cheerful way of life as branches of olives, 'for to make cheerful the face of us in oil', as the psalm-singer says, and again: 'Be slaves to the Lord in gladness.' Let us lift again in the inside man the divine and spiritual [noun continues in the next section]…
pass_b_english: …meditation, patience, and endurance. “He has blessed your children within you” (Psalm 147:13). These are the faithful infants who received the Lord with the branches, that is, with new fruits, who nurse on the milk of Christ’s teaching. For as soon as they believe in Him, they praise, they sing hymns, they give glory, as it is written: “Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babies You have prepared praise” (Psalm 8:2; Matthew 21:16).

Let us become a holy mount for Him in place of the unclean colt, so that He may ride upon us. Let us yoke the chariot of our thoughts to Him, “and He will reign” over us “forever, and of His kingdom there will be no end” (Luke 1:33).

Let us take up a cheerful way of life like olive branches, “to make our face cheerful with oil” (Psalm 104:15), as the psalmist says, and again: “Serve the Lord with gladness” (Psalm 100:2). Again, let us carry in the inner man the divine and spiritual…

review.scope: every clause of the section, checked against translations/hilr_u02_rem_source.json (PG 93, Khazarzar text)
notes: Coverage: every clause from μελέτη to πνευματικὴν is rendered; nothing added. The row opens and closes mid-sentence, so the English carries an ellipsis at both ends.
Agency and mood: the hortatory subjunctives (Γενώμεθα, Ζεύξωμεν, Λάβωμεν, Ἄρωμεν) are 'let us'; ἐπιβῇ is the purpose clause with Christ as subject; βασιλεύσει is future.
Scripture verified against the verses with LXX Psalm numbers converted: Psalm 147:13 (LXX 147:2), Psalm 8:2 (LXX 8:3) with Matthew 21:16, Luke 1:33, Psalm 104:15 (LXX 103:15), Psalm 100:2 (LXX 99:2).
Reviewer fix applied before assembly: 'and who suck the milk' became 'who nurse on the milk'.
Source numbers '5' (line or page mark) and '13' (section number) are not part of the text and are left out, as in the neighbouring rows.
Pronouns for Christ are capitalised (He, Him, His), as in the rest of the book.
translator_notes: The row opens mid-list: μελέτη, μακροθυμία, ὑπομονή continue the 'bars of your gates' list (faith, hope, love) that closes u02-open, so the English starts with an ellipsis. The u02-open English currently ends that list with a full stop after 'love'; a reviewer may want to change it to a comma and ellipsis so the two rows join.

The row ends mid-sentence: θεϊκὴν καὶ πνευματικὴν takes its noun ἐργασίαν ('work') from the start of u02-rem-mid, so the English ends with an ellipsis. The current u02-rem-mid English ('Let us work as the palm trees…') does not reflect this split clause; the joined sense is 'let us carry in the inner man the divine and spiritual work, like the palm branches of the date palms'.

Scripture, with LXX Psalm numbering converted: Psalm 147:13 = LXX 147:2 ('He has blessed your children within you'; υἱούς rendered 'children', as in standard English versions, because the next clause explains them as infants); Psalm 8:2 = LXX 8:3, as quoted in Matthew 21:16; Psalm 104:15 = LXX 103:15; Psalm 100:2 = LXX 99:2. Luke 1:33 is Gabriel's promise, adapted from 'over the house of Jacob' to 'over us'; only the quoted words sit inside the quotation marks.
ὄχημα rendered 'mount' (a thing one rides), since it stands against πῶλος, the colt; ἐπιβῇ 'ride upon'. ἅρμα is 'chariot', which picks up u01-rem-close's 'chariots of Ephraim'.

ἱλαρὰν πολιτείαν / ἱλαρῦναι: Hesychius plays on ἱλαρός ('cheerful'). Both are rendered with 'cheerful' to keep the play, and ἐλαιῶν / ἐλαίῳ (olive / oil) keeps the second link. ἔσω ἄνθρωπος is 'inner man', the term already used in u01-rem-close.
μελέτη rendered 'meditation' (the steady pondering of Psalm 1:2); μακροθυμία 'patience'; ὑπομονή 'endurance'.
Source numbers '5' (line or page marker) and '13' (section number) are omitted, as in the neighbouring rows.
Capitalisation follows u02-open: He/Him/His for Christ. Note for the reviewer: u02-open cites 'Praise the Lord, Jerusalem' as Psalm 148:13, but the verse is Psalm 147:12 (LXX 147:1).

source_text:
μελέτη, μακροθυμία, ὑπομονή. «Εὐλόγησε τοὺς υἱούς σου ἐν σοί», οἵτινές εἰσι τὰ
πιστὰ νήπια τὰ δεξάμενα τὸν κύριον μετὰ τῶν κλάδων, τουτέστι μετὰ καρπῶν νέων,
τὰ θηλάζοντα τὸ γάλα τῆς διδασκαλίας τοῦ Χριστοῦ· πιστεύοντες γὰρ εἰς αὐτὸν
εὐθέως αἰνοῦσιν, ὑμνοῦσιν, δοξολογοῦσιν, καθὼς γέγραπται· «Ἐκ στόματος νηπίων
καὶ θηλαζόντων κατηρτίσω αἶνον.» Γενώμεθα αὐτῷ ὄχημα ἅγιον ἀντὶ ἀκαθάρτου
πώλου, ἵνα ἐπιβῇ ἐφ' ἡμᾶς. Ζεύξωμεν αὐτῷ τὸ ἅρμα τῶν λογισμῶν ἡμῶν, «καὶ
βασιλεύσει» ἐφ' ἡμᾶς «εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, καὶ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔσται τέλος.»
5
13 Λάβωμεν ἱλαρὰν πολιτείαν ὡς κλάδη ἐλαιῶν, «τοῦ ἱλαρῦναι τὸ πρόσωπον
ἡμῶν ἐν ἐλαίῳ», καθώς φησιν ὁ ψαλμῳδός, καὶ πάλιν· «∆ουλεύσατε τῷ κυρίῳ ἐν
εὐφροσύνῃ.» Ἄρωμεν πάλιν ἐν τῷ ἔσω ἀνθρώπῳ τὴν θεϊκὴν καὶ πνευματικὴν
